description: In **1968**, **Stanley Kubrick** transforms science fiction into a sensory experience. Few dialogues, precise images, and one question: what becomes of humans in the face of their tools?

hero.hook: A nearly wordless film that redefined science fiction forever.

blocks.text: *2001: A Space Odyssey*, released in **1968**, remains the great monument of science fiction in cinema. Its director, **Stanley Kubrick**, rejects the talky action film. It offers an experience: images, music, silence. From prehistory to space, he questions the place of humans in the universe.
More than fifty years later, the film has barely aged. For what ? Because it focuses on visual precision rather than fashion effects.

**Stanley Kubrick** (1928-1999) wants to master everything: script, editing, camera lenses. This requirement runs through his career, from war films (*The Paths of Glory*) to horror (*Shining*). For *Barry Lyndon*, he will even adapt  optics designed for the , in order to film using candlelight alone. [[Zeiss]] [[NASA]]

blocks.caption: The black monolith: a silent presence that restarts human evolution.

blocks.text: At Kubrick, every detail counts. The decor is not a background. It’s a filmed idea.

sections.title: Kubrick, the man of total control

blocks.text: In **1964**, Kubrick contacted writer . Together, they start from a short story, , to invent a film and a novel in parallel. Clarke brings the scientific vision. Kubrick brings visual abstraction. [[Arthur C. Clarke]] [[“The Sentinel”]]
Before computers, each effect was made by hand. For the final journey, supervisor Douglas Trumbull invents : a technique that creates hypnotic tunnels of light. [[slitting scan]]
The budget, enormous for the time, financed rotating sets and models with almost documentary precision. The result doesn't look like a gimmick. It looks like a credible future.

sections.title: Clarke, Trumbull and magic before digital

blocks.text: At the heart of the film: , the on-board computer. We see it almost only as a red eye. HAL must complete the mission while hiding his true nature from the crew. Caught in this contradiction, he chooses to eliminate humans. [[Artificial intelligence and HAL 9000]]

blocks.caption: HAL 9000: a soft voice, a unique look, deadly logic.

blocks.text: Kubrick does not film an “evil” robot. He films a tool that reveals our own flaws. Humans create machines that are too powerful, then discover that they no longer control them.

sections.title: HAL 9000, the tool that becomes a threat

blocks.text: The ending abandons the classic story for an abstract journey, up to the image of the “Star Child”, an astral fetus. The music structures everything: the waltz of  (*The Beautiful Blue Danube*) makes the space stations dance;  (*Thus spoke Zarathustra*) marks the great leaps in evolution. [[Johann Strauss]] [[Richard Strauss]]
*2001* has elevated science fiction to the level of meditation. Few dialogues, many images: Kubrick films human evolution as a mystery, not as a lesson.
